# CLI reference

`oa` is the command-line client of the REST API. For login, the config file and worked examples see [CLI](../integrations/cli.md); for shell completion see [Shell completion](../integrations/cli.md#shell-completion). Global flags may go anywhere on the command line. Long flags take two dashes (`--format json`); put a name that starts with `-` after a bare `--` (`oa repo show -- -legacy`).

## Usage

```text
oa [flags]
```

## Global flags

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--format` | `string` | Output format: table or json (default "table") |
| `--server` | `string` | Server URL (default http://localhost:8080, env OA_SERVER) |
| `--token` | `string` | API token (env OA_TOKEN) |
| `--version` | none | Print the version |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Named by |
|---|---|
| `OA_GPG_PASSPHRASE` | `oa gpg import` |
| `OA_IMPORT_SOURCE_TOKEN` | `oa import artifactory`, `oa import nexus` |
| `OA_IMPORT_SOURCE_URL` | `oa import artifactory`, `oa import nexus` |
| `OA_IMPORT_SOURCE_USER` | `oa import artifactory`, `oa import nexus` |
| `OA_SERVER` | `--server` |
| `OA_TOKEN` | `--token`, `oa oidc exchange` |
| `OA_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | `oa webhook create`, `oa webhook repo create` |

## Auth

### `oa auth`

Sign in, sign out and manage tokens.

#### `oa auth login`

Sign in and save the credentials.

Sign in with a username and password (prompted, or --password-stdin) and save an API token, or leave the username blank to paste an existing API token.

```text
oa auth login [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--password-stdin` | none | Read the password from stdin |
| `--server` | `string` | Server URL (default: the global server) |
| `--username` | `string` | Username (required with --password-stdin) |

#### `oa auth logout`

Forget the saved credentials.

```text
oa auth logout [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--password-stdin` | none | Read the password from stdin (with --revoke) |
| `--revoke` | none | Also revoke the saved token on the server (needs --username and --password-stdin) |
| `--username` | `string` | Username (with --revoke) |

#### `oa auth passwd`

Change your password.

```text
oa auth passwd [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--password-stdin` | none | Read current then new password from two lines on stdin |

#### `oa auth token`

Manage API tokens.

#### `oa auth token create`

Create an API token (signs in with the account password).

Create an API token. The server refuses to mint tokens for a caller that authenticates with a token, so the account password is asked for (or read with --password-stdin).

```text
oa auth token create --name <name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--kind` | `string` | Token kind: access\|deploy (default "access") |
| `--name` | `string` | Token name |
| `--password-stdin` | none | Read the account password from stdin |
| `--username` | `string` | Account to sign in as (default: the saved token's owner) |

#### `oa auth token list`

List your API tokens.

```text
oa auth token list [flags]
```

#### `oa auth token revoke`

Revoke an API token (signs in with the account password).

```text
oa auth token revoke <id> [--username U] [--password-stdin] [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--password-stdin` | none | Read the account password from stdin |
| `--username` | `string` | Account to sign in as (default: the saved token's owner) |

#### `oa auth whoami`

Show the signed-in user.

```text
oa auth whoami [flags]
```

## Repositories and packages

### `oa artifact`

List, upload and delete packages in a repository.

#### `oa artifact delete`

Delete a package by id.

```text
oa artifact delete <repo> <id> [flags]
```

#### `oa artifact list`

List packages in a repository.

```text
oa artifact list <repo> [flags]
```

#### `oa artifact upload`

Upload a file to a hosted repository.

Upload one file to a hosted repository; the repository's format picks the upload endpoint. Flags may come before or after the arguments.

--presigned uploads straight to the object store through a presigned URL (raw repositories); files above 5 GiB switch to it automatically, in parts. --path, --content-type, --multipart, --part-size and --parallel need --presigned. --branch, --apk-repo and --arch address the directory of an .apk upload.

```text
oa artifact upload <repo> <file> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--apk-repo` | `string` | Alpine repository directory of an .apk upload (default main) |
| `--arch` | `string` | Architecture directory of an .apk upload; needed for noarch packages |
| `--branch` | `string` | Alpine branch directory of an .apk upload (default edge) |
| `--content-type` | `string` | Content type (--presigned; default: detected by the server) |
| `--multipart` | none | Upload in parts at any size (--presigned; automatic above 5 GiB) |
| `--parallel` | `int` | Parts uploaded at the same time, 1 to 16 (--presigned, multipart) (default 4) |
| `--part-size` | `size` | Part size such as 128M, 1G or a byte count, 5M to 4000M (--presigned; implies --multipart; default: chosen by the server) |
| `--path` | `string` | Artifact path in the repository (--presigned; default: the file name) |
| `--presigned` | none | Upload straight to the object store through a presigned URL (raw repositories) |

Examples:

```text
oa artifact upload files ./release.tar.gz
oa artifact upload files ./disk.img --presigned --path images/disk.img --part-size 128M --parallel 8
oa artifact upload alpine ./pkg.apk --branch v3.20 --apk-repo community --arch aarch64
```

### `oa cleanup`

Manage cleanup policies.

#### `oa cleanup create`

Create a cleanup policy (needs --keep-count or --keep-days).

```text
oa cleanup create <repo> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--enabled` | none | Enabled (--enabled=false to disable) (default true) |
| `--keep-count` | `int` | Keep the newest N versions of each package |
| `--keep-days` | `int` | Keep versions newer than N days |
| `--name` | `string` | Policy name |
| `--name-pattern` | `string` | Regular expression selecting the package names the policy applies to |
| `--schedule` | `string` | Cron schedule (5 fields) |

#### `oa cleanup delete`

Delete a cleanup policy.

```text
oa cleanup delete <repo> <id> [flags]
```

#### `oa cleanup list`

List cleanup policies.

```text
oa cleanup list <repo> [flags]
```

#### `oa cleanup run`

Run a cleanup policy now.

```text
oa cleanup run <repo> <id> [flags]
```

#### `oa cleanup show`

Show a cleanup policy.

```text
oa cleanup show <repo> <id> [flags]
```

#### `oa cleanup update`

Update a cleanup policy (only the flags you pass are sent).

```text
oa cleanup update <repo> <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--enabled` | none | Enabled (--enabled=false to disable) (default true) |
| `--keep-count` | `int` | Keep the newest N versions of each package |
| `--keep-days` | `int` | Keep versions newer than N days |
| `--name` | `string` | Policy name |
| `--name-pattern` | `string` | Regular expression selecting the package names the policy applies to |
| `--schedule` | `string` | Cron schedule (5 fields) |

### `oa repo`

Manage repositories.

#### `oa repo create`

Create a repository.

Create a hosted repository. --format is required and names the package format.

After the command name, --format is the repository format; to choose the output format put the global flag before the command: oa --format json repo create NAME --format npm.

```text
oa repo create <name> --format <fmt> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--description` | `string` | Description |
| `--format` | `string` | Repository format (required) |
| `--honour-quay-expiry` | none | Hosted docker repositories: delete images once their quay.expires-after time has passed (not with --immutable-releases) |
| `--immutable-releases` | none | Block deleting or overwriting released versions |
| `--public` | none | Public repository |
| `--sign-packages` | none | Hosted rpm repositories: sign uploaded RPMs with the active GPG key |
| `--trash-retention-days` | `string` | Days deleted items stay in the trash (0 = delete immediately, default = server setting) |

#### `oa repo delete`

Delete a repository (moved to the trash; prompts for the name on a terminal).

```text
oa repo delete <name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--confirm` | `string` | Repository name, as confirmation |

#### `oa repo list`

List repositories.

```text
oa repo list [flags]
```

#### `oa repo members`

List the member repositories of a group repository.

```text
oa repo members <name> [flags]
```

#### `oa repo packages`

List packages in a repository.

```text
oa repo packages <name> [flags]
```

#### `oa repo show`

Show repository details.

```text
oa repo show <name> [flags]
```

#### `oa repo update`

Update a repository (only the flags you pass are sent).

```text
oa repo update <name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--description` | `string` | Description |
| `--honour-quay-expiry` | none | Hosted docker repositories: delete images once their quay.expires-after time has passed (--honour-quay-expiry=false to stop) |
| `--immutable-releases` | none | Block deleting or overwriting released versions (--immutable-releases=false to allow) |
| `--merge-proxy-versions` | none | Group repositories, administrators only: merge proxy members' versions of names a hosted member holds (--merge-proxy-versions=false restores hosted-wins) |
| `--public` | none | Public (--public=false to make private) |
| `--sign-packages` | none | Hosted rpm repositories: sign uploaded RPMs with the active GPG key (--sign-packages=false to stop) |
| `--trash-retention-days` | `string` | Days deleted items stay in the trash (0 = delete immediately, default = server setting) |

### `oa search`

Search repositories and packages.

Search repositories and packages by name. Several words are joined into one query; flags may come before or after the query.

```text
oa search <query>... [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--fmt` | `string` | Filter by format |
| `--limit` | `int` | Max results (default 50) |
| `-r`, `--repo` | `string` | Filter by repository |

### `oa trash`

List, restore and purge deleted items.

#### `oa trash list`

List trashed items.

List every trashed item (administrators) or, with --repo, those of one repository (repository delete permission).

```text
oa trash list [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--kind` | `string` | Only items of this kind (e.g. maven_artifact, docker_tag, repository) |
| `-r`, `--repo` | `string` | Only items of this repository |

#### `oa trash purge`

Permanently delete trashed items.

Permanently delete one trashed item (administrators):

```text
  oa trash purge <kind> <id> [--yes]
```

or empty the trash of one repository (repository manage permission):

```text
  oa trash purge --repo NAME --all [--yes]
```

Both ask for confirmation unless --yes is given; without a terminal --yes is required.

```text
oa trash purge <kind> <id> | --repo NAME --all [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` | none | Purge every trashed item of --repo |
| `-r`, `--repo` | `string` | Repository whose trash to empty |
| `-y`, `--yes` | none | Do not ask for confirmation |

#### `oa trash restore`

Restore a trashed item.

```text
oa trash restore <kind> <id> [--repo NAME] [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-r`, `--repo` | `string` | Restore through this repository's trash (not for kind repository) |

## Administration

### `oa audit`

Read and export the audit log (admin).

#### `oa audit export`

Export the audit log (default: jsonl to stdout).

Export the audit log as jsonl (default) or csv, to stdout or to the --output file.

After the command name, --format is the export format; the global output format is not used by this command.

```text
oa audit export [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--action` | `string` | Filter by action |
| `--actor` | `string` | Filter by actor |
| `--format` | `string` | Export format: jsonl\|csv (default "jsonl") |
| `-o`, `--output` | `string` | Write to this file instead of stdout |
| `--since` | `string` | Only entries at or after this time (RFC 3339, YYYY-MM-DD or an age like 24h, 7d) |
| `--until` | `string` | Only entries before this time (same forms) |

#### `oa audit list`

List audit entries.

```text
oa audit list [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--action` | `string` | Filter by action |
| `--actor` | `string` | Filter by actor |
| `--limit` | `int` | Max entries (default 50) |

### `oa gpg`

Manage GPG signing keys (admin).

#### `oa gpg activate`

Make a key the signer (global or per deb/rpm repository).

```text
oa gpg activate <key> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--repository` | `string` | Repository to activate for (default: global) |

#### `oa gpg deactivate`

Stop using a key for signing.

```text
oa gpg deactivate <key> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--repository` | `string` | Repository to deactivate for (default: global) |

#### `oa gpg delete`

Delete a key (id, name or fingerprint).

```text
oa gpg delete <key> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--force` | none | Delete even if the key is active or assigned |

#### `oa gpg export`

Export the public key.

```text
oa gpg export <key> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--output` | `string` | Write the public key to FILE (default: stdout) |

#### `oa gpg generate`

Generate a signing key.

```text
oa gpg generate [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--activate` | none | Make the key the active signing key |
| `--algorithm` | `string` | Algorithm: ed25519\|rsa4096 (default "ed25519") |
| `--comment` | `string` | User ID comment |
| `--email` | `string` | User ID email |
| `--name` | `string` | Key name |
| `--no-activate` | none | Do not activate the key |
| `--user-name` | `string` | User ID name |

#### `oa gpg import`

Import a private key (passphrase: stdin or env OA_GPG_PASSPHRASE).

```text
oa gpg import --key <file|-> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--activate` | none | Make the key the active signing key |
| `--key` | `string` | Armored private key file, or - for stdin |
| `--name` | `string` | Key name |
| `--no-activate` | none | Do not activate the key |
| `--passphrase-stdin` | none | Read the key passphrase from stdin (env: OA_GPG_PASSPHRASE) |

#### `oa gpg list`

List GPG keys.

```text
oa gpg list [flags]
```

#### `oa project update`

Update a project (only the flags you pass are sent).

Update a project. --display-name and --description need the owner role; the policy flags (--allowed-formats, --allowed-repo-types, --repo-name-prefix, --allow-public-repos, --max-repositories, --token-max-ttl-days) need a global admin.

```text
oa project update <name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--allow-public-repos` | none | Allow public repositories (global admin) |
| `--allowed-formats` | `string` | Comma-separated formats; empty = all (global admin) |
| `--allowed-repo-types` | `string` | Comma-separated repo types: hosted,proxy,group (global admin) |
| `--description` | `string` | Description (owner) |
| `--display-name` | `string` | Display name (owner) |
| `--max-repositories` | `int` | Maximum repositories, 0 = unlimited (global admin) |
| `--repo-name-prefix` | `string` | Required repository name prefix (global admin) |
| `--token-max-ttl-days` | `int` | Maximum token lifetime in days, 0 = no cap (global admin) |

### `oa bundle`

Manage release bundles.

#### `oa bundle add`

Add artifacts to a draft bundle, by path, by image digest or by the build that produced them.

Add artifacts to a draft bundle: either --repo R with one or more --path P, --repo R with one or more image manifest digests (--digest sha256:..., docker repositories), or --from-build NAME/NUMBER (optionally limited to the repositories named by --repo).

```text
oa bundle add <name> <version> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--digest` | `stringArray` | Image manifest digest sha256:... in the docker --repo (repeatable) |
| `--from-build` | `string` | Add every artifact recorded for build NAME/NUMBER (properties build.name and build.number) |
| `--path` | `stringArray` | Artifact path in --repo (repeatable) |
| `-r`, `--repo` | `stringArray` | Repository of the artifacts (repeatable with --from-build to limit the search) |

#### `oa bundle check`

Report external checks on a bundle.

#### `oa bundle check report`

Report the result of an external check (a policy run, a scan) on a bundle.

Set the state of the check NAME on the bundle NAME VERSION. A promotion stage that lists the check in its required_checks only promotes the bundle once the check is success. The caller needs write access on the bundle's repository (a deploy token is enough). Reporting a check again replaces its state.

```text
oa bundle check report <name> <version> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--details-url` | `string` | Link to the full report (a PipelineRun, a Conforma report) |
| `--expires-at` | `string` | RFC 3339 time after which the result no longer counts |
| `--name` | `string` | Check name, as the stage's required_checks lists it (required) |
| `--status` | `string` | Check state: pending, success, failure, error (required) |
| `--summary` | `string` | One line describing the result |

Create a draft release bundle.

```text
oa bundle create <name> <version> [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--description` | `string` | Bundle description |
| `--pipeline` | `string` | Promotion pipeline, by name (needed to promote the bundle later) |

Seal a bundle (optionally sign its manifest).


| Flag | Value | Description |

#### `oa bundle show`


### `oa check`

Check a lockfile's dependencies against a repository before installing.

Read the package versions a lockfile pins (composer.lock, package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json) and ask the repository, usually the group your package manager uses, whether it will serve each of them: available, held (by a curation rule, the minimum age, a quarantine or the license policy, with the reason), not_found or unknown (a proxy that has not cached the package's metadata yet). Local, linked, bundled and git or file dependencies are skipped. Reading needs read access on the repository.

A proxy only knows the packages it has fetched, so on a fresh proxy most answers are unknown. --fetch first requests each package's metadata through the repository, as the package manager would, so the proxies behind it fetch and cache it from their upstreams; then it checks.

The exit status is 1 when a dependency is held or not found (or unknown, with --fail-on-unknown) and 0 otherwise; the result is printed either way (--format json for every dependency).

```text
oa check <repo> --lockfile FILE [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--fail-on-unknown` | none | Exit 1 also when the repository cannot tell (unknown) |
| `--fetch` | none | First request each package's metadata through the repository, so its proxies cache it |
| `--lockfile` | `string` | Lockfile to check: composer.lock, package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json |
| `--no-dev` | none | Skip the dependencies the lockfile marks as development only |

Examples:

```text
oa check php --lockfile composer.lock
oa check npm-all --lockfile package-lock.json --no-dev
oa check php --lockfile composer.lock --fetch
```

### `oa gate`

Check whether an artifact may ship: vulnerabilities, licences, quarantine, attestations.

Ask the server for the gate of one artifact of a repository: either the manifest or artifact with --digest sha256:..., or the vulnerability scan --scan ID. The answer lists every check behind the verdict. Reading it needs read access on the repository.

The exit status is 0 when the gate passes and 1 when it does not; the result is printed either way (--format json for the full document).

```text
oa gate <repo> --digest D | --scan ID [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--digest` | `string` | Digest of the artifact or image manifest (sha256:...) |
| `--scan` | `string` | Id of a vulnerability scan of the repository |

### `oa oidc`

Exchange CI identity tokens for access tokens.

#### `oa oidc exchange`

Trade a CI job's OIDC token for a short-lived deploy token.

Read the OIDC ID token of a CI job (a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI token, a Kubernetes projected service account token) from --token-file and exchange it, at the server's trust policies, for a short-lived deploy token. The token is printed on stdout.

With --docker-config DIR the token is also stored in DIR/config.json as the registry credential of the server's host, so docker, cosign, oras and skopeo can use it (set DOCKER_CONFIG=DIR); other hosts already in the file are kept.

No stored credential is involved: the exchange is anonymous and --token and OA_TOKEN are not sent.

```text
oa oidc exchange [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--docker-config` | `string` | Also write the token as registry credential into DIR/config.json |
| `--policy` | `string` | Trust policy to use, by name (default: the one that matches the token) |
| `--token-file` | `string` | File holding the ID token, or - for stdin (required) |

Promote a sealed bundle to a pipeline stage.


| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--notes` | `string` | Promotion notes |
| `--stage` | `string` | Pipeline stage to promote to (required) |
| `--target-repo` | `string` | Repository to promote into (default: the one the stage fixes) |

### `oa upload`

Upload files to a hosted repository and set build properties.

Upload files to a deb, ivy, maven, raw, rpm or sbt repository (and the other formats that take a package file) and set build properties on them.

Quiet on stdout except for its result: one JSON document under --format json. Exits non-zero on the first failure with the reason on stderr.

```text
oa upload <repo> <file|glob>... [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--build-name` | `string` | Build name, recorded as property build.name |
| `--build-number` | `string` | Build number, recorded as property build.number |
| `--build-url` | `string` | Build URL, recorded as property build.url |
| `--flat` | none | Drop the local directories: upload every file by its name |
| `--property` | `stringArray` | Property k=v set on every uploaded artifact (repeatable) |
| `--target-path` | `string` | Path in the repository; a trailing / makes it a directory (default: the file's path) |
| `--vcs-revision` | `string` | Source revision, recorded as property vcs.revision |
| `--version` | `string` | Package version, for the formats whose file does not say (composer: when composer.json has no "version") |

## Configuration and migration

### `oa apply`

Apply declarative manifests to the server.

Apply the manifests given with -f (files, directories or - for stdin) so the server matches them.

Exit status 0 on success, 1 on error.

```text
oa apply -f FILE|DIR|- [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--continue-on-error` | none | Keep applying after a failure (exit status is still 1) |
| `-f`, `--file` | `stringArray` | Manifest file, directory or - for stdin (repeatable) |
| `--force-secrets` | none | Send every secret even if the server reports it as set |
| `--kind` | `stringArray` | Only consider this kind (repeatable), e.g. Repository |
| `-o`, `--output` | `string` | Output format: json (default: human readable) |
| `--prune` | none | Delete objects previously applied by oa that are no longer in the manifests |
| `--prune-all` | none | Delete every object absent from the manifests, managed or not (never seeded objects; Users and ServiceAccounts only with --kind User or --kind ServiceAccount) |
| `-R`, `--recursive` | none | Descend into subdirectories of -f directories |
| `--validate-only` | none | Validate the manifests offline and exit |

### `oa diff`

Show what apply would change.

Show what `oa apply` would change for the manifests given with -f.

Exit status 0 when nothing changes, 2 when there are changes, 1 on error.

```text
oa diff -f FILE|DIR|- [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | `stringArray` | Manifest file, directory or - for stdin (repeatable) |
| `--force-secrets` | none | Send every secret even if the server reports it as set |
| `--kind` | `stringArray` | Only consider this kind (repeatable), e.g. Repository |
| `-o`, `--output` | `string` | Output format: json (default: human readable) |
| `--prune` | none | Delete objects previously applied by oa that are no longer in the manifests |
| `--prune-all` | none | Delete every object absent from the manifests, managed or not (never seeded objects; Users and ServiceAccounts only with --kind User or --kind ServiceAccount) |
| `-R`, `--recursive` | none | Descend into subdirectories of -f directories |

### `oa export`

Export the server configuration as manifests.

Export the server configuration as declarative manifests that `oa apply` takes: one YAML stream on stdout, or one file per object with --output DIR.

```text
oa export [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--kind` | `stringArray` | Only export this kind (repeatable); User is exported only when named |
| `-o`, `--output` | `string` | Write one file per object into this directory (default: one YAML stream on stdout) |
| `--with-members` | none | Include fields normally omitted, such as Group members |

### `oa import`

Import from another artifact manager.

#### `oa import artifactory`

Import from Artifactory.

Import repositories from another artifact manager into this server.

Every --repo SRC[:DST] maps one source repository to a destination repository (DST defaults to SRC); an openartifact source also takes --all for every hosted repository. The source credentials come from --source-user and --source-token-file (or OA_IMPORT_SOURCE_USER and OA_IMPORT_SOURCE_TOKEN), never from the command line.

Exit status 0 when everything was imported, 1 when some assets failed, 2 on a usage error.

```text
oa import artifactory --source-url URL --repo SRC[:DST]... [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` | none | openartifact source: import every hosted repository, under the same name |
| `--artifactory-listing` | `string` | Artifactory listing mode: aql or storage (default "aql") |
| `--concurrency` | `int` | parallel transfers (default 4) |
| `--create-repos` | none | create missing destination repositories (hosted, matching format) |
| `--deb-component` | `string` | fallback Debian component when the source does not say |
| `--deb-distribution` | `string` | fallback Debian distribution when the source does not say |
| `--dry-run` | none | print the plan without writing anything |
| `--formats` | `string` | with --all: only repositories of these formats (comma-separated) |
| `--path-prefix` | `string` | only import assets whose repository path starts with this prefix (e.g. com/acme/) |
| `--properties` | `string` | properties to copy: comma-separated keys or prefix* patterns, 'none' to disable (default "deb.*,rpm.*,build.name,build.number,vcs.*") |
| `--quiet` | none | only print the summary |
| `--repo` | `SRC[:DST]` | repository to import as SRC or SRC:DST (repeatable) (default []) |
| `--retries` | `int` | retries after a transient failure of a source request or an upload (0 disables) (default 3) |
| `--retry-max-wait` | `duration` | longest wait between retries; a Retry-After above it is not waited out (default 30s) |
| `--source-token-file` | `string` | file holding the source token/password, '-' for stdin (or OA_IMPORT_SOURCE_TOKEN) |
| `--source-url` | `string` | base URL of the source system (or OA_IMPORT_SOURCE_URL) |
| `--source-user` | `string` | source user name (or OA_IMPORT_SOURCE_USER) |
| `--state-file` | `string` | resume file: completed assets are skipped on the next run |

#### `oa import config`

Migrate the configuration of another instance as manifests.

```text
oa import config [flags]
```

|---|---|---|

## Utility

### `oa completion`

Generate the shell completion script.

#### `oa completion bash`

Generate the bash completion script.

Generate the bash completion script. It needs the bash-completion package.

Load it in the current shell:

```text
  source <(oa completion bash)
```

Install it for every session:

```text
  oa completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/oa   # one user
  oa completion bash | sudo tee /etc/bash_completion.d/oa              # all users (Linux)
  oa completion bash > "$(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/oa"     # macOS with Homebrew
```

Start a new shell for it to take effect.

```text
oa completion bash [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | none | Complete names without descriptions |

#### `oa completion fish`

Generate the fish completion script.

Generate the fish completion script.

Load it in the current shell:

```text
  oa completion fish | source
```

Install it for every session:

```text
  oa completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/oa.fish
```

Start a new shell for it to take effect.

```text
oa completion fish [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | none | Complete names without descriptions |

#### `oa completion powershell`

Generate the PowerShell completion script.

Generate the PowerShell completion script.

Load it in the current session:

```text
  oa completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

Install it for every session by adding that line to your PowerShell profile ($PROFILE).

```text
oa completion powershell [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | none | Complete names without descriptions |

#### `oa completion zsh`

Generate the zsh completion script.

Generate the zsh completion script.

If completion is not enabled in your zsh yet, enable it once:

```text
  echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc
```

Load it in the current shell:

```text
  source <(oa completion zsh)
```

Install it for every session:

```text
  oa completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_oa"                                  # Linux
  oa completion zsh > "$(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_oa"    # macOS with Homebrew
```

Start a new shell for it to take effect.

```text
oa completion zsh [flags]
```

| Flag | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | none | Complete names without descriptions |

### `oa version`
